title: prefill vs decode: chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage-overlap pipeline optimizations
author: Jun Park
description: Context: The current prefill->decode pipeline has observable head-of-line and GPU kernel underutilization for mixed-length requests. This PR implements a set of coordinated runtime changes: (1) chunked prefill to split long prefill sequences into smaller prefill chunks that can be overlapped with decode work, (2) speculative prefill where we pre-execute likely upcoming KV-cache entries for short-horizon tokens, and (3) stage-overlap scheduler changes to permit prefill and decode kernels to run in a pipelined fashion when safe. Motivation: reduce end-to-end p99 latency and improve overall GPU throughput on real inference workloads (chat + long-context summarization). This PR contains implementation, microbenchmarks, regression guards, and rollout plan.

diff_summary: Key changes (high-level): added a ChunkedPrefill abstraction to split large prefill runs into smaller tasks; scheduler now recognizes "stage overlap" regions and allows decode kernels to execute speculatively on completed chunks; speculative KV-cache fills are enqueued based on n-gram heuristics collected from recent traffic; continuous batching updated to coalesce chunk boundaries to avoid micro-batches thrashing kernels. Small API additions: PrefillTask, ChunkDescriptor, SpeculativeFillPolicy. No public API surface changes for the Redwood API. Unit tests + integration tests added.
benchmarks: Microbenchmarks (internal perf harness) on rdx-gpu-n1 (A100 equivalent): - Chat workload (avg tokens/request 48): throughput +24% and p95 latency -12% - Long-context summarization (avg prefill 2048 tokens): end-to-end throughput +32%, p99 latency down 18% - Tail test (mixed lengths): GPU utilization improved from 68%->87% and average kernel idle time reduced by ~45%. Notes: gains dominated by reduced idle time during large prefill windows and better packing of small decode requests into kernel slots.
testing_and_ci: CI: full unit suite + integration tests + perf-canary run. All checks passed on CI; perf-canary run shows stable improvements. Testing notes: added deterministic fake-kernel harness for stage overlap to validate correctness under interleaved prefill/decode sequences. Stress test: 1M requests simulating PLG traffic over 6 hours; no memory leaks observed.
rollout_notes: Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime flag 'prefill_stage_overlap' (off by default). 2) Canary on Dedicated pool (10% capacity) for 24h with perf monitors. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics stable. Rollback: flip feature flag off; scheduler will fallback to legacy prefill pipeline. Migration: KV-cache speculative fills are local-only and do not modify persisted cache format.
compatibility_and_risks: Compatibility: No client-visible API changes. Risk: speculative prefill may increase short-term memory pressure and can cause extra GPU work on mispredictions. Mitigations: conservative default heuristic (only speculatively fill up to 8 future tokens for chat workloads), adaptive disable if mem pressure or misprediction rate exceeds thresholds, per-tenant flags. Kernel scheduler changes have been validated against our correctness matrix.
release_notes: Performance: Prefill/decode pipeline optimizations - chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage-overlap scheduling improve GPU utilization and reduce tail latency for mixed workloads. Default gated; opt-in via runtime flag. See docs/perf/prefill-decode-optimizations.md for details.
review_comments: Samantha Lee (review): Nice work. Two safety questions: (1) do we have a hard upper bound on speculative fills per request to avoid OOMs? (2) Can the scheduler block on a chunk boundary and create a deadlock with continuous batching?

Jun Park (author): Answered — speculative fills limited to 8 tokens by default and per-tenant cap enforced; scheduler uses non-blocking fences and the continuous-batcher coalesces chunk boundaries to avoid deadlocks. Added tests simulating blocking patterns.
Rohan Gupta (review): Observed a slight perf regression on a microcase (many tiny requests). Can we add an adaptive path to disable stage-overlap for extremely tiny mean lengths?
Jun Park (author): Added adaptive threshold: if avg prefill length < 12 tokens over 1s window, overlap disabled. Measured no regressions after change.
Maya Thompson (approver): Verified correctness on integration harness and canary. Approving for merge.
